British Values
The DfE have reinforced the need “to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.”
At Walwayne Court Primary School we uphold and teach pupils about British Values which are defined as:
These values are taught explicitly through Personal, Social, Health and Emotional (PSHE), and Religious Education (RE). We also teach British Values through planning and delivering a broad and balanced curriculum.
At Walwayne Court School we will actively challenge pupils, staff or parents expressing opinions contrary to fundamental British Values, including ‘extremist’ views.
At Walwayne Court these values are reinforced regularly and in the following ways:
Wow! What a buzz around the school! We have voted for and elected our School Council. As a school we were incredibly proud of all the children that took part and spoke in front of their classes, in order to receive a nomination. A huge well done to our successful candidates.

pageCache.text:
Vision, Aims & Values
Together we are stronger. We learn together with smiles on our faces because we believe that happy children learn.
Our vision charter has been created in collaboration with a range of stakeholders and can be found in the document below.

Welcome to Walwayne Court School
This site aims to give you a taste of what it means to be part of the Walwayne Court Primary School community.
The members of our school make this a special place in which children can grow into young citizens who are happy, kind to each other, confident and academically ready to take on the world and embrace the challenges that lie ahead.
Our values of love, mutual respect, tolerance and kindness permeate everything that we do at Walwayne Court. These values apply to all members of our community: children, staff, governors, parents, grandparents and volunteers alike, ensuring that this school is a happy place to come to.
We pride ourselves in offering a curriculum that excites our children and inspires a love of learning. Alongside our focus on the basic skills of reading, writing and maths, we ensure that all of our children access an enormous variety of learning opportunities especially relating to the arts subjects. Visitors to our school are always impressed by the vibrant atmosphere, the imaginative artwork and the positive attitude that our children display.

pageCache.pageTitle: Walwayne Court School - Extra Curricular Clubs
pageCache.text:
Extra Curricular Clubs
Breakfast Club
The before school enrichment club runs Monday to Friday from 7.30am to 8.40am by our teaching assistants; Mrs Rolls and Mrs Stenton. The children are able to take part in a range of activities including art, ICT, reading and lots more.
The cost per day is currently £4.00. Breakfast is served for children arriving before 8am, which includes cereal or toast with a drink.
Between 7.30am and 8.00am children should be dropped off at the rear hallway door. After 8.00am children should be dropped off at the back door of Ladybirds classroom. Bookings are made via scopay, and should be made at least 2 days in advance, however, some days sessions are fully booked, so we advise booking a term at a time. We are unable to accept children who arrive on the day who are not booked in, the only exception to this is a family emergency (e.g. a family member being taken ill). Sessions that are cancelled within 24 hours of the club starting will not be refunded.
After School Enrichment Club
Our after school club is there to provide support for working parents. The club is run by a group of our teaching assistants and the children can participate in activities such as art, board games and reading.
The first session is 3.05pm until 4.15pm, the second session is 4.15pm until 5.30pm. There are two sessions on each day Monday - Thursday, and one session on Friday. You can book one or two sessions, or if your child is attending an after school activity club, you can book the second session only.
The cost per session is currently £4.00 for the first session, and £4.50 for the second session, which includes a snack and a drink, or children may bring their own snack if preferred.
The children are taken to the club at the end of the school day. The pick up point is Ladybirds class. The children use the school grounds when there is good weather so may not be in the classroom, so please only pick up at the end of each session, not part way through a session so you know where to find them! Please arrive promptly to collect your child; persistent late collections can result in the second session being charged, or a late collection fee added to your account.
Bookings are made via scopay, and should be made at least 2 days in advance, however, some sessions are fully booked, so we advise booking a term at a time. We are unable to accept children who are not booked in, the only exception to this is a family emergency (e.g. a family member being taken ill). Sessions that are cancelled within 24 hours of the club starting will not be refunded.
Activity Clubs - bookable every two terms
At Walwayne Court we strive to offer a wide range of clubs to all the children. Some of our clubs are provided by outside agencies while others are run by school staff. Towards the end of each term a letter informing parents of the clubs available for the forthcoming terms will be sent home which need to returned before the end of the term so that places can be allocated. We try to ensure that all those children who wish to attend a club will be offered at least one club of their choice. Clubs in the past have included football, netball, multi skills, dance, art, mindfulness, magic and many more! An updated list can be obtained via the school office.
We always welcome new ideas, and would love to hear from you if you have any suggestions, or are able to provide a club.

Music Tuition
During the school day, we are able to offer music tuition in a range of instruments for children from Years 2 to 6. These are provided by private teachers.
The instruments available are:
Woodwind (flute, clarinet, saxophone, recorder)
Towards the end of every school year, a letter is sent home to all the children who will be in Years 2 to 6 in the subsequent year, in order for music tuition applications to be completed. We usually manage to accommodate children’s first choice. Music fees are charged termly in advance and are paid directly to the relevant teacher. Each teacher sets their own fees and terms and conditions. A term’s notice is usually required to terminate the agreement. Learning an instrument does take serious commitment and regular practise at home is required to make good progress.

Safeguarding
"Staff are well trained to recognise the signs of a pupil at risk of harm. They know how to report a concern. Leaders respond to concerns quickly. They work with external agencies to support pupils and their families successfully." Ofsted 2022
If you are concerned about the well-being or safety of a particular child, please do not hesitate to contact Sharon Turley in order to discuss your concerns further. Alternatively, you could also contact either the Local Authority Children's Services Department at County Hall or the NSPCC.
Walwayne Court School is committed to ensuring that all staff and adults with responsibility for children's safety and welfare are trained to deal with incidents involving aggressive behaviour and only use physical intervention as a last resort, in line with DfE and LA advice. If used at all, it will be in the context of a respectful, supportive relationship with the pupil and in accordance to the guidance within the Behaviour Policy and the Code of Conduct for Safeguarding of Children, all of which are available for download from below. We will aim to ensure minimal risk of injury to pupils and staff. We actively support the Government's Prevent Agenda to counter radicalism and extremism.
Our Designated Safeguarding Lead is our Head Teacher Mrs Sharon Turley.
The Deputy Designated Safeguarding Leads are Mrs Lauren Rowe (SENCO), Mrs Julie Collier (Office Manager) and Mrs Rhiannon Purnell (Teacher and Pastoral lead).
If you believe a child to be at immediate risk please call 999.
Please use South West Grid for Learning Report it e-safety page to report harmful online content.
The latest information regarding Keeping Children Safe in Education can be found here:
Keeping Children Safe in Education
To report a safeguarding concern please email: safeguarding@walwaynecourt.wilts.sch.uk

Attendance
If you request leave for your child to attend a medical appointment or for a holiday please complete the absence request form. If you have any queries please refer to the attendance policy on our school website or alternatively ask for a paper copy at the school office. We please ask that non-urgent dental appointments to be made after school or alternatively during school holiday time. For more information on the Government guidelines regarding school attendance and absence please click here. The link will take you to the Government webpage on this topic.
Documents
Absence due to Illness
In the event of absence, please let the school know by phoning on the first day of absence before 9:30am, and on each subsequent day until your child is well enough to return. We do have an answer-phone so messages can be left at any time on 01225 776886. Alternatively we can be emailed at admin@walwaynecourt.wilts.sch.uk. Notification of absence is most important for safeguarding and we ask that you comply with this request at all times. If your child is absent and we have not received an explanation, we will attempt to contact you. If we do not receive a reason for absence within 14 days, the absence will be recorded as 'unauthorised'. Please ensure ALL contact details are up to date so we can contact you immediately should there be an emergency.
If you are unsure as to how long your child should be off school due to infectious illness please refer to the document below for information. There is also some great advice on whether a child is well enough for school in the document below which has been put together by the NHS.

Snow and bad weather policy
Should the school be closed due to exceptional weather conditions an email or a text will be send to parents/carers as soon as a decision is made regarding closure. You can also listen to the reports on BBC Wiltshire Radio here

E-Safety
Always be careful when you are using the internet. It can help you to keep in touch with your friends and help your education – but it can also cause harm – to you and to others.
Remember help is always available at school if you are having any problems online.
Don’t be afraid to talk to your teacher or another adult at school.
If you or anyone you know is worried about Child Exploitation, Online Protection or anything related to Internet safety please click the link below which will take you to the CEOP reporting website:
Helpful links to look at with your family
Age 5-7Age 8-10Age 11-13
Tips for staying safe online:
Make sure you keep new online friends strictly online. If someone you don't know asks to be your online friend you must ensure an adult knows about it.
Know how to use the CEOP Button and how to report it to the CEOP Centre if you are concerned about someone’s online behaviour towards you.
Child friendly privacy policy
